_comment: UDCAP-NATIVE binding file (controller_type: udcap).
Why this exists in addition to bindings_index.json:
UDCAP advertises ``compatibility_mode_controller_type: "knuckles"``
in UDCAP_profile.json so that legacy Index-only apps still see a
controller.  But the compat layer only bridges a SUBSET of inputs
(typically just trigger value + grip, for the basic Index emulation).
The per-finger curl channels and the skeletal channel — which UDCAP
DOES populate natively at /input/finger/* and /input/skeleton/* —
are NOT bridged through the knuckles compat layer.
Result: bindings_index.json loads cleanly for our app, every entry
passes validation, but UDCAP returns 0 for every finger and
bActive=False for skeletal.  The fix is to ALSO ship a binding
with ``controller_type: "udcap"`` so SteamVR routes the action
reads through UDCAP's native input handling.  When both are
present, SteamVR prefers the binding whose controller_type matches
the device's NATIVE type (udcap > knuckles compat).
Differences from bindings_index.json:
* controller_type: "udcap" (not knuckles)
* Includes /input/finger/thumb (UDCAP exposes 5 fingers; Index has 4)
* Trigger/grip use UDCAP-native paths /input/trigger and /input/grab
bound as ``button`` with ``click`` input (UDCAP exposes these as
discrete events, not analog values, per UDCAP_profile.json)
description: UDCAP-native binding: skeleton + 5-finger curl + trigger/grip click
name: UST Teleop — UDCAP native (5-finger + skeletal)
